properties.statement:
A PROPERTY THAT NAMES A NODE ID IS ACCEPTED WITHOUT CHECKING THE NODE EXISTS — while an EDGE to the same missing node is refused by sixteen helpers and a dedicated test file. The guard was built for one shape of reference and the other shape has none.

MEASURED 2026-08-16, and found sideways rather than by looking: `create_node` was called for a TemporalFact carrying `subject_id: "cap:questions-are-tracked"`. It was written and echoed back with no complaint. `get_node(Capability, "cap:questions-are-tracked")` then returned `{node: null}` — THE CAPABILITY HAS NEVER EXISTED. The id was invented while writing the node, and nothing objected. Corrected to `cmp:detect` only because the write was read back on the habit AGENTS.md prescribes; nothing in the tool's own reply would have revealed it.

⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING IS THE CONTRAST, not the slip. `ver:edges-need-both-ends` is an unusually thorough guard: an edge to a missing node is refused through ALL SIXTEEN typed helpers, with an atomicity case, a size-floor so the table cannot shrink, and a mutation check that found fourteen of sixteen depend on the shared guard. That work exists because `authored_by` once accepted `person:anthony`, which was never created, and a phantom AUTHORED_BY sat in the graph until somebody noticed BY EYE. ⇒ The identical failure is still reachable through a PROPERTY, and it lands in the same place: a dangling reference nothing reports.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY THE SAME BUG: an edge endpoint is structurally a reference and the schema knows it. A property is a string, and the schema does not record that `TemporalFact.subject_id` MEANS a node id — so there is nothing for a generic guard to key on. Any fix needs the schema to say which properties are references before validation can act, which is a real change rather than an oversight to patch.

BLAST RADIUS, NOT ESTABLISHED and stated as such: `subject_id` is the case measured. Other properties across the schema plausibly name nodes the same way (`ABOUT_ENTITY` has an edge for this, which is the modelled route, so the property may be the redundant one) — nobody has enumerated them, and the count of already-dangling values across this design is unknown and unmeasured.
